intro: Sport needs more than players. It needs rooms, rule books and the bodies that run them. This unit looks at two kinds of institutions. The first is disability sport: the Deaflympics, wheelchair basketball, the Paralympic Games and Special Olympics. The second is the set of public bodies that built Illinois fields and gyms, from park commissions to the IHSA.

Illinois appears in both stories. Galesburg hosted the first national wheelchair basketball tournament in 1949. Soldier Field hosted the first Special Olympics Summer Games in 1968. Chicago built field houses in 1905, but for decades some beaches were closed to Black residents by custom. People changed those rules through laws, courts, protests and votes.

By the end, you will be able to name the bodies that run disability sport and explain what classification does. You will be able to explain who owns and runs a public gym in Illinois. You will also be able to use dates and documents to argue how the doors to these rooms opened.
bigQuestion: How do public bodies decide who gets to play, and how have people changed those decisions?

timeline.t: The Land Ordinance reserves section 16 of each township for public schools
Illinois creates three park commissions for Chicago
The IHSA begins as a body for Illinois high schools
Chicago's South Park Commission opens ten neighborhood parks with field houses
Eugene Williams dies at a Chicago beach, and a week of rioting follows
Deaf athletes from nine nations meet in Paris for the International Silent Games
Twenty-two park districts join to form the Chicago Park District
The National Wheelchair Basketball Association is founded at Galesburg, Illinois
The first Paralympic Games are held in Rome
The first Special Olympics Summer Games open at Soldier Field in Chicago
Illinois voters approve a new constitution that lets school and park districts share services
The Americans with Disabilities Act becomes law

words.d: an organization that writes a sport's rules, runs its events and keeps its records
the world games for deaf athletes, begun in Paris in 1924 and named Deaflympics in 2001
describing the world games for athletes with physical and visual impairments, first held in 1960
a group of Paralympic athletes whose impairments affect their sport in a similar way
a trained official who places an athlete in a sport class
the sports movement for people with intellectual disabilities, begun at Soldier Field in 1968
the part of the 1973 Rehabilitation Act that bans disability discrimination in federally funded programs
a square of land six miles on a side, with 36 sections, from the 1785 survey
a park building with gyms, showers, meeting rooms and sometimes a library
a local government with an elected board and taxes that runs parks and recreation
separation of people by race through custom and pressure rather than written law
a group of schools sorted by size so each group has its own state title

test.q: Which body, founded in 1924, runs games for deaf athletes?
choices: the deaf sports committee, now the ICSD
test.why: CISS, now the ICSD, was founded in 1924 and runs the Deaflympics.

test.q: Who hosted the first National Wheelchair Basketball Tournament in 1949?
choices: Tim Nugent of the University of Illinois
test.why: Tim Nugent hosted the tournament at Galesburg, where the NWBA was founded.

test.q: Where were the first Paralympic Games held in 1960?
test.why: The 1960 Games in Rome are counted as the first Paralympics.

choices: places an athlete in a sport class
test.why: Classifiers decide which sport class an athlete belongs in.

test.q: Which city hosted the first Special Olympics Summer Games?
test.why: They opened at Soldier Field in Chicago on July 20, 1968.

test.q: When was the International Paralympic Committee founded?
test.why: The IPC was founded in Düsseldorf in 1989.

test.q: Which law bans disability discrimination in programs that receive federal money?
test.why: Section 504, passed in 1973, covers federally funded programs, including school sports.

test.q: What did the Land Ordinance of 1785 set aside in each township?
test.why: Section 16 of each township was reserved for schools.

test.q: Which Chicago bodies were created by the state in 1869?
test.why: The South, West and Lincoln Park commissions were created in 1869.

test.q: Under the 1970 Illinois Constitution, what may school districts and local governments do?
choices: contract with each other to share services and property
test.why: Article VII, Section 10 lets them make intergovernmental agreements, such as sharing a gym.

test.q: What was de facto segregation at Chicago's beaches in 1919?
choices: a state law requiring separate beaches
separation by custom and threat, with no written rule
test.why: No written rule divided the 29th Street beach; custom and violence did.

test.q: What did the 2013 letter from the Office for Civil Rights tell schools?
choices: give students with disabilities an equal chance to try out and play
build a new gym in every town
test.why: The letter explained Section 504 in school sports, including reasonable modifications.

test.q: What did Watson v. City of Memphis (1963) require?
test.why: The Supreme Court ordered Memphis to open its parks to all at once.

test.q: How do IHSA rules get changed?
choices: Member schools propose and vote on by-laws
test.why: The IHSA is a voluntary association whose member schools vote on its by-laws.

test.q: How are the IHSA and the Chicago Park District different?
choices: The IHSA runs beaches; the park district runs state finals
The IHSA is an association of schools; the park district is a local government
test.why: Schools join the IHSA by choice, while the Chicago Park District is a unit of local government with taxes.

write.prompt: Pick one room or games from this unit, such as a Chicago beach, a field house, the Galesburg tournament or the first Special Olympics. Who decided who could use it, and how did that change? Name at least two dates and two documents, laws, bodies or records from the unit.
tips: Name each document or law with its year, such as the Americans with Disabilities Act of 1990.
Say which body made each decision: a park board, a federation, a court or member schools.
Tell what happened before and after the change.
Use unit words like governing body, sport class or de facto segregation.
Compare two cases instead of judging people.
